items.title: How Fishes Live in an Ice-Covered Ocean
items.abstract: The Arctic Ocean lies at the northernmost point of our planet, where the sun does not set in summer and does not rise in winter, and where temperatures are cold enough to keep your ice cream frozen. Floating on top is a sheet of sea ice that expands in winter and shrinks in summer. For Arctic animals, living in this environment means dealing with extremes in temperature, sea ice, light, and food.
